newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CRICKET-W.P AND NATAL SET FOR LAST DAY THRILLER.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-W.P AND NATAL SET FOR LAST DAY THRILLER.

text.p: New Supersport Series champions Natal played themselves into a position to end their season with victory over Western Province after an intriguing third day's play at Newlands on Sunday.
Natal restricted the defending champions to 215 for nine in their second innings and will hope to face a target of no ore than 300 for victory on Monday.
Dale Benkenstein's side clinched the title with their first batting bonus point on Saturday and gutsily moved on to 359 -- a deficit of 74 on first innings -- before they were bowled out on Sunday.
Derek Crookes top-scored with 96 and there were useful contributions from Errol Stewart (44) and Andrew Hudson (32) before Natal's bowlers took over.
They reduced Province to 38-4 and 58-5 before half-centuries from Craig Matthews (64) and Brian McMillan (63) restored the innings with an 88-run seventh wicket partnership.
McMillan -- who is expected to be named in South Africa's squad for the second test against Australia when it is announced on Monday -- got in useful batting practice with a three-hour knock.

However test opener Gary Kirsten again failed, collecting a third ball duck as did Desmond Haynes in his final first class match. The 41-year-old West Indian batsman was well caught at third slip by Derek Crookes but still left the field to a tanding ovation.

Jacques Kallis (14) and Herschelle Gibbs (20) could not repeat their heroics of Saturday which saw them post a Western Province third wicket record stand of 257 as Natal clawed their way back into the game after conceding 433 runs in the first innings
